title: Where the Floor Stops
summaryZh: 伊萬回到游泳池,站在深水區的線前面。他想起了六歲那年的一件事,而佩特拉問了他一個他從來沒被問過的問題。

sentences.text: There is a line painted on the floor of the town pool.
sentences.zh: 鎮上游泳池的池底畫著一條線。

sentences.text: On one side the water is one metre deep, and on the other it is three.
sentences.zh: 線的一邊水深一公尺,另一邊三公尺。

sentences.text: Ivan stood with his toes against that line for a long time.
sentences.zh: 伊萬腳趾抵著那條線,站了很久。

sentences.text: The rest of the class had already gone past it without discussing it.
sentences.zh: 班上其他人早就越過去了,沒有人討論這件事。

sentences.text: He was six years old the first time he understood what deep water was.
sentences.zh: 他第一次明白什麼叫深水,是六歲那年。

sentences.text: It was a river, not a pool, and it was the summer his family moved.
sentences.zh: 那是一條河,不是游泳池,那年夏天他們全家搬了家。

sentences.text: An older boy pushed him from a rock, probably without meaning anything by it.
sentences.zh: 一個大一點的男孩從石頭上把他推下去,大概沒什麼惡意。

sentences.text: Somebody pulled him out within a few seconds, and nobody talked about it afterwards.
sentences.zh: 幾秒鐘之內就有人把他拉了上來,事後也沒有人再提。

sentences.text: For thirty-five years Ivan had described himself as a person who never learned.
sentences.zh: 三十五年來,伊萬一直說自己是那種「沒學過」的人。

sentences.text: Petra swam over and rested her arms on the edge beside him.
sentences.zh: 佩特拉游了過來,手臂靠在他旁邊的池邊。

sentences.text: She did not tell him that the water was safe, or that he was ready.
sentences.zh: 她沒有告訴他水很安全,也沒有說他準備好了。

sentences.text: She asked him a question that nobody had ever asked him about it.
sentences.zh: 她問了他一個關於這件事、從來沒有人問過他的問題。

sentences.text: "What do you think is going to happen?"
sentences.zh: 「你覺得會發生什麼事?」

sentences.text: Ivan opened his mouth and found that he did not have a sentence ready.
sentences.zh: 伊萬張開嘴,發現自己並沒有現成的句子可以說。

sentences.text: He had carried the fear for so long that he had never taken it out to look at.
sentences.zh: 他把這份恐懼帶了太久,久到從來沒有拿出來看過。

sentences.text: "I will go under," he said at last, "and nobody will notice."
sentences.zh: 「我會沉下去,」他終於說,「而且沒有人會發現。」

sentences.text: Petra nodded as though this were a completely reasonable thing to say.
sentences.zh: 佩特拉點了點頭,好像這是一句完全合理的話。

sentences.text: "That is the part I can fix," she said. "I will notice. That is my job."
sentences.zh: 「這部分我可以解決,」她說。「我會發現。那是我的工作。」

sentences.text: It was such a small answer that Ivan almost laughed at it.
sentences.zh: 那個回答小到伊萬幾乎要笑出來。

sentences.text: He had expected to be told that his fear was not real.
sentences.zh: 他本來以為對方會說,他的恐懼不是真的。

sentences.text: Instead she had agreed with the fear and then answered it.
sentences.zh: 結果她先同意了那份恐懼,然後才回答它。

sentences.text: He crossed the line, and for two strokes it was exactly as bad as he had imagined.
sentences.zh: 他越過了那條線,前兩下划水,真的和他想像中一樣糟。

sentences.text: His feet reached down for a floor that was no longer there.
sentences.zh: 他的腳往下探,想找一個已經不在那裡的池底。

sentences.text: Then he remembered to blow out slowly, which was the very first lesson.
sentences.zh: 然後他想起來要慢慢把氣吐出來——那是第一堂課教的。

sentences.text: The water held him up, the way it had been holding him up for nine weeks.
sentences.zh: 水把他撐了起來,就像過去九個星期一直撐著他那樣。

sentences.text: He swam eight metres, turned around badly, and swam eight metres back.
sentences.zh: 他游了八公尺,笨拙地轉了個身,又游了八公尺回來。

sentences.text: When he stood up in the shallow end his hands were shaking.
sentences.zh: 他在淺水區站起來時,雙手在發抖。

sentences.text: The man of sixty said well done, and then went back to his own lengths.
sentences.zh: 那位六十歲的男士說了聲「做得好」,然後回去游他自己的。

sentences.text: Nobody clapped, and Ivan was grateful for that.
sentences.zh: 沒有人鼓掌,伊萬很感謝這一點。

sentences.text: He is not a good swimmer now, four months later.
sentences.zh: 四個月後的現在,他還是游得不好。

sentences.text: He is a slow one, and his legs still sink when he gets tired.
sentences.zh: 他游得很慢,累的時候腳還是會往下沉。

sentences.text: But he goes on Tuesdays, and he swims in the three-metre water.
sentences.zh: 但他每個星期二都去,而且在三公尺深的水裡游。

sentences.text: What changed was not his body, and it was not really his courage either.
sentences.zh: 改變的不是他的身體,其實也不是他的勇氣。

sentences.text: Somebody had asked him what he thought would happen, and had waited for the answer.
sentences.zh: 有人問了他覺得會發生什麼事,而且真的等他把答案說出來。

sentences.text: Thirty-five years, and the question had taken about four seconds to ask.
sentences.zh: 三十五年,而那個問題問出口只花了大約四秒鐘。

questions.q: What happened to Ivan when he was six years old?
options: He was pushed into a river and pulled out again
He failed a swimming test at the town pool
He watched somebody else get into difficulty

questions.q: What was Ivan actually afraid of?
options: Being the slowest swimmer in his class
Discovering that he could not float at all

questions.q: Why did Petra's answer work on him?
options: She accepted the fear instead of denying it, then answered it
She promised that nothing bad could ever happen in a pool
She told him the deep end was not really three metres
